findings.title: "Mark all as read" wipes the edition with no way back
findings.what: The double-check icon in the top bar marks every story read at once, with no confirmation. The full-screen "Fin." page then slides over everything, and the only way back, the Undo message, is hidden underneath it.
findings.where: The Daily, 390 and 884, day and night · #mr click www/index.html:11299 · finShow :7428 · #toast z-index 95 vs #fin z-index 2000
findings.why: The first icon a curious new reader taps erases their first edition and shows a "Fin." screen with no visible undo.
findings.fix: Put the Undo message above the Fin page (one z-index line), and do not show Fin from mark-all when nothing was actually read; optionally ask "Mark 24 stories as read?" when more than a handful are affected.
findings.risk: Low for the stacking fix; medium for a confirmation box (tests click the button directly).

findings.title: Back on the "Fin." page leaves the app
findings.what: With the Fin page open, pressing Back (what the Android back button does inside the app) does not close it; the app is left instead. The reader, Settings and the side drawer all close correctly on Back because they register themselves as a layer; Fin does not.
findings.where: Fin page, any width · finShow www/index.html:7428 has no pushLayer('fin') · popstate handling :16161-16170
findings.why: Being thrown out of the app right after finishing an edition feels like a crash.
findings.fix: Register Fin as a layer when it opens and close it on Back, copying the existing pattern used by the gallery and year-in-review pages.
findings.risk: Low; copies an existing pattern. Confirm on a phone (headless used history.back()).
findings.noMock: No mockup: this is behavior, not pixels.

findings.title: Onboarding tells readers the swipe directions backwards
findings.what: The last onboarding page says "Swipe a story right to save it, left to mark it read." The app does the opposite (right = mark read, left = save). The in-app tip that appears later states it correctly.
findings.where: Onboarding step 5, 390/884 · www/index.html:13402 · correct wording in TIPQ :12494
findings.why: The very first instruction a new reader gets is wrong, so their first swipe does the opposite of what they meant.
findings.fix: Change the sentence to "Swipe a story right to mark it read, left to save it."

findings.title: An inline "Read more:" line cuts the rest of the story off, silently
findings.what: When a story has a short "Read more: …" promo line in its middle (common on BBC, Guardian, Independent and WordPress sites), the cleaner treats that line as the end of the article and throws away everything after it. The chopped story is then counted as complete, so no "Partial story" label appears.
findings.where: Reader, all widths/modes · tidy rule 2 www/index.html:8932 (once 35% of the text has passed, any short line matching END ends the story) · END list :8767 includes "read more" · ENDMARK :9066 makes looksIncomplete say "complete"
findings.why: The second half of ordinary news stories vanishes with no warning.
findings.fix: Only treat a short "end" line as the end when little text follows it (for example under a quarter of the story, or fewer than two real paragraphs); otherwise drop just that one line. This is a cleaning rule, not the fetch strategy, but it is extraction logic, so it is your call.
findings.risk: Medium: extraction heuristic; run the reader tests afterwards.

findings.title: The Daily's photo cover never shows its photo
findings.what: One day in three the Daily picks a photo cover when the lead story has a picture. The photo never appears on phone or Fold: the crop pass written for the other cover styles treats the full-bleed photo as the wrong shape, shrinks it to a small box and places it beneath the morning/evening artwork, so readers only ever see the artwork.
findings.where: The Daily › Today, 390 and 884, day/night, every theme · coverCrop www/index.html:6078 selector includes '#grid .dcov' · inset gets zIndex -1 at :6102/:6107 while the art SVG (.dcv-art, CSS :2974) paints over it · dayCoverHtml :15091
findings.why: A whole cover treatment is dead: on the day the Daily promises a photo cover there is no photo.
findings.fix: Leave the Daily cover out of the crop pass (drop '#grid .dcov' from that selector) so it keeps its designed full-bleed photo. Then re-check Newsprint, where a bright photo makes the edition line hard to read: give it the normal shade gradient on photo covers.
findings.risk: Low-medium: the crop pass was written for the other cover styles; tests/cover_crop.js only covers those. Confirm on a phone.

findings.title: The "saved offline" dot covers the story's age (also reported as F-06)
findings.what: The small round "saved on this device" badge is drawn over the last item of the card footer. In text rows it sits exactly on the time stamp ("1h" becomes "⬇h", "30m" becomes "⬇m"); in Fold two-column cards it also covers the end of the summary. Seen in Daily (Next up, Also in this issue), Headlines, Sunday, All Stories, site and folder pages.
findings.where: 390/884/1100, day and night · .rdy www/index.html:880 (absolute, right 10px bottom 10px) over #grid .card .cfoot time :3946 · :2671 already pads .also rows for this but not .cfoot · measured 10px overlap at 390
findings.why: The age of a story is the one fact a news list exists to show.
findings.fix: CSS only: give footers (and the summary) room on the right when a card carries the badge, or move the badge into the footer flow so it takes its own space.

findings.title: Cypress theme, day: site name is white on a near-white card
findings.what: In the Cypress theme by day, the site name next to the avatar is white on an almost white card, so it is invisible, in the Daily's Quick Reads strip cards and on every phone Compact card. Night is fine.
findings.where: 390/884 day · rule www/index.html:2550 (halcyon .noimg cards: white .src) beats :774 · measured white on rgb(255,253,246)
findings.why: Readers cannot see where a story comes from.
findings.fix: Exclude the Quick Reads strip cards and Compact cards from that white-text rule (one selector change).

findings.title: A broken site says "No stories yet" instead of what went wrong (also S-04)
findings.what: Open a single site whose feed is broken (server error, or a web page instead of a feed) and the page says "No stories yet — A few sites didn't answer, and the rest haven't sent new stories", then "Stories are on the way… still sending" while retrying. On a one-site page that is untrue, and the app already knows the real reason ("Beta's server had a problem", "What Beta sent wasn't a readable feed"), which it shows correctly in Manage your sites. An empty-but-valid feed is described as "wasn't a readable feed".
findings.where: Site page s:… , 390 day/night · render0 www/index.html:6374-6376 returns empNoStories() (:12136, counts all feeds, ignores the selected one) before the error banner at :6380 · feedReason :16126 · retry loop :5852
findings.why: The reader is told to Refresh when the real answer is "this site is down" or "this address isn't a feed".
findings.fix: In the empty branch, when a single site is selected and it failed, show that site's real reason with Try again; describe a feed with zero items as "sent an empty feed".

findings.title: Phone Compact cards keep an empty photo column for text-only stories
findings.what: On the phone, Compact cards without a photo still reserve a 72-96px photo column: the text is pushed to the right and a blank block sits beside it. Fold width is fine.
findings.where: 390 day and night · grid columns www/index.html:4456 · :4613 removes the letter tile but not the column · measured "72px 252px"
findings.why: Every text-only story wastes a quarter of the row and looks unfinished.
findings.fix: CSS only: one column for Compact cards without a photo.

findings.title: Back cover says "you read what mattered" when nothing was read
findings.what: The Daily's back cover can say "Plenty of tech today, and you read what mattered." with zero stories read.
findings.where: Daily end card · phrase f10 www/index.html:13947 has topic:1 but no state:'done' guard (f4/f11/f12 have one) · via pe('finish') from dayEndCard :8298
findings.why: A sentence that is plainly untrue makes the whole edition feel scripted.
findings.fix: Add the same "only when done" guard to that one phrase.

findings.title: Site page says "8 unread." right above "8 stories · 8 unread"
findings.what: On a single-site page the masthead line "8 unread." sits directly above "8 stories · 8 unread".
findings.where: .fm-s www/index.html:3264 (mastHtml :7482) and wireRender :6723
findings.why: Repeated numbers read as clutter.
findings.fix: Hide the first line when it only repeats the count.

findings.title: Fold/tablet Daily front page ends in a lonely "Next up · 1 story" under two rules
findings.what: At 884 and 1100 the Daily front page ends with "Next up · 1 story" under two stacked 3px rules; at 1100 the right half of the lead row is empty with only the rule.
findings.where: 884/1100 · .nr-mid www/index.html:2396 + .nr-rail border · nrBlocks :7626, nrLH :7612, rail forced full width by :2473
findings.why: Looks like a layout leftover rather than a section.
findings.fix: Fold a one-story rail into the lead's sub-list, or hide that block under 1240px.

findings.title: "Sections" sheet counts disagree with the header in Cards view
findings.what: In All Stories Cards view the Sections sheet says 15 + 20 stories while the header says 40 and "Last hour" actually holds 17 rows; the stories mixed in from other sources are not counted. Columns view counts correctly.
findings.where: headings built www/index.html:6686 · sheet :8170
findings.why: Numbers that do not add up erode trust in the list.
findings.fix: Count the mixed-in stories into their section.

findings.title: Short but complete stories are labeled "Partial story"
findings.what: A complete story of about 150-250 words that ends with a full stop is labeled "PARTIAL STORY — This may be only the start of the story." Anything under 400 words without an explicit end phrase gets the label.
findings.where: looksIncomplete www/index.html:9067 · flag set :9101 · label written :9667 · fixtures of 130/165/213/250 words all badged at 390 and 884
findings.why: Wire briefs and notices are routinely 100-300 words; the badge cries wolf and readers stop believing it.
findings.fix: For a story's own page text of 120+ words, require a real sign of a cut (no final punctuation, an ellipsis, or a "read more / subscribe" tail) before labeling; keep the 400-word rule only for the behind-the-scenes rescue search.
findings.risk: Medium: the same flag drives the rescue search; soften only the label branch.

findings.title: Share rows and raw markdown leak into story bodies
findings.what: A share row shows as a line of underlined links ("Share on Facebook Tweet Email"), and raw markdown stays as typed: "## What the plan does", "* Adds three…", "[ ]" and "[x]" lines.
findings.where: tidy rule 1 www/index.html:8915-8925 only matches "share this" / "follow" · isolateExtras :8777 and junkClean :7004 do not normalize #, *, -, [ ]
findings.why: Junk in the body is the fastest way to make a reader doubt the whole app.
findings.fix: Treat short link-only "share/tweet/email" lines as junk; turn "## " into a subheading, "* " into a bullet and drop "[ ]" markers in one pass over the paragraphs.

findings.title: Code blocks in Pages mode scroll sideways and steal the page swipe
findings.what: In Pages mode a code block is one long line that scrolls sideways, cut at the right edge under the Copy button with no hint; a sideways swipe over it scrolls the code instead of turning the page.
findings.where: .cols .body pre www/index.html:128 (white-space:pre; overflow:auto) overrides the wrapping rule at :1336 · measured 1564px wide in a 346px frame
findings.why: Readers of tech sites get stuck on a page that will not turn.
findings.fix: Let code wrap inside the reader's columns (one CSS rule), or keep the scroll but add a right-edge fade.

findings.title: Web version: "Best available" voice never actually picks a voice
findings.what: In a browser (not the Android app) the automatic voice choice never happens: it always falls back to the engine's default voice, possibly in another language or a remote one, even when a matching local voice exists. The check requires a quality score that only the Android voice list has.
findings.where: bestVoice www/index.html:10088 'if(!c.length||!c.some(v=>v.q))return null' · q only set by the plugin in loadVoices :10118 · voice/lang then unset at :9990 and :15578
findings.why: Read-aloud on the web sounds worse than it needs to, or speaks in the wrong language.
findings.fix: Drop the quality-score requirement; rank by score, then default, then local; set the language from the browser when none is set.
findings.noMock: No mockup: a code path; headless browsers have no voices.

findings.title: A story that opens with a number gets a drop cap on the digit
findings.what: A story beginning "2024 was the warmest…" shows a giant "2" followed by "024 was" in small caps.
findings.where: makeDropcap www/index.html:13671 accepts digits · decorate0 :13696
findings.why: Looks like a typesetting mistake.
findings.fix: Exclude digits from the drop-cap rule.

findings.title: Lead photo crops from the middle, so faces near the top are cut
findings.what: The reader's lead photo is cropped from the center. A portrait with a face in the top third shows chin and shoulders only. Covers already favor the upper part of a photo; the reader does not.
findings.where: .cols>.hsf img.hero www/index.html:1581 (default object-position 50% 50%) · 346×190 frame for a 600×1000 photo at 390 · covers use 50% 22% (:1937) and 50% 30% (:1189)
findings.why: Cropped faces look careless.
findings.fix: One CSS line: position the photo at 50% 25%.
findings.risk: Low. Checked with a synthetic portrait (the test fixture is a flat color).

findings.title: Web version: Read aloud says "No voices" and starts anyway
findings.what: In a browser, tapping Read aloud with no voices shows "No voices are installed…" and then starts: the button flips to Pause, the player docks, nothing plays.
findings.where: ttsToggle www/index.html:10041 returns after the toast only on Android or when forced
findings.why: A player that says it cannot play and plays silently is confusing.
findings.fix: On the web, wait up to a second for the voice list; if still empty, show the message and stop; otherwise start without the message.

findings.title: Photo covers draw the photo twice on phones
findings.what: On phones the contained-photo covers (Magazine at 390; Clean/Magazine at 884; Index/Journal with tall photos) show a sharp inset photo and a second full-size sharp copy behind it. The copy behind should be frosted, but Smooth mode (the default on touch devices) turns off every blur, leaving an unblurred photo under a plain gradient.
findings.where: Daily, cover style Magazine, 390 · .cover.ctn www/index.html:3838-3840 · blur removed by html.smooth * {backdrop-filter:none} :2921 · S.smooth default in applyFx :15705
findings.why: Looks like a double-photo rendering mistake.
findings.fix: CSS: in Smooth mode give the contained cover a flat tinted backdrop (or a pre-blurred copy) instead of the sharp photo.

findings.title: Paper-cover labels are too faint to read
findings.what: On the Daily paper cover the small labels above the cover lines ("BEFORE BED · BETA") are 9.5-11px at 70% opacity: 2.96:1 contrast in Cypress day, 3.13 Aurora, 2.25 Dynamic, 3.21 Coast (4.5:1 is the floor for small text). A Cypress gold override exists but never applies because a generic rule outranks it.
findings.where: .dcov .dcv-l small www/index.html:2988 · opacity .7 at :3621 · dead override :4296
findings.why: Readers with ordinary eyesight squint at the cover's own table of contents.
findings.fix: Full opacity for those labels and fix the override's ranking. Measured after: 5.9:1 Cypress, 4.9-5.1 Coast.

findings.title: Coast and Sepia Rosewood day: site names are too light
findings.what: In Coast and Sepia Rosewood by day, the site name and section label on every card use the accent color at 11px: 2.65-2.82:1 in Coast, 2.89-3.06 in Rosewood. Badge plates themselves are correctly tinted in every theme; only these two day accents are too light.
findings.where: .src .sn/.ssec color var(--a2) www/index.html:2592 · --a2 at :2568 (coast) and :2572 (rosewood)
findings.why: Source labels are the second thing a reader looks at.
findings.fix: A darker day tone for those labels in the two themes (Coast #b8432a → 4.55:1, Rosewood #7f5d1c → 4.87:1).

findings.title: Reader kicker line is too faint in Cypress, Coast and Rosewood day
findings.what: The small line above a story's headline ("ALPHA · IN BRIEF · 2 MIN", 10.5-12px) measures 3.07:1 in Cypress day, 3.36 Coast, 3.45 Rosewood, 4.17 Dynamic. In Cypress a darker brass exists for it but the generic rule wins.
findings.where: .kick www/index.html:105 · #rd .cols .kick color var(--rbr) ~:4190 · --rbr #7d5f14 :4186 vs fallback :4185
findings.why: The source and reading time are hard to read on every story.
findings.fix: Use the darker day tones (Cypress #7d5f14 → 5.86:1, Coast #b8432a → 5.42, Rosewood #7f5d1c → 5.49).

findings.title: Coast day gray text is below the readability floor
findings.what: Coast's day gray (#5D7A80) measures 3.63-3.86:1 on summaries, "2 min read" and the Brief intro. Rosewood day (4.1-4.4) and Dynamic day (3.9) on tinted cards are borderline; Cypress is 4.46.
findings.where: html[data-theme=coast] --mut www/index.html:2568 · rosewood :2572 · Dynamic --mut :2319
findings.why: Summaries are most of what a reader reads in the list.
findings.fix: Darker grays: Coast #4a666c (5.17:1 measured), Rosewood #6a524c (5.81); Dynamic derives its gray from the ink color.

findings.title: Sunrise/sunset card covers the hint message
findings.what: The sunrise/sunset card that plays on a light/dark switch and the hint message share the bottom-left corner; the card covers the message's first words for about 4 seconds.
findings.where: .sky www/index.html:934 · #toast :1163
findings.why: Minor, but the hint is unreadable exactly when it is shown.
findings.fix: Lift the sky card while a message is showing (one CSS rule).

findings.title: Faint ghost text behind the story header (needs phone confirmation)
findings.what: In the themes sweep, faint paragraph text from a later page showed through behind the story header about 2.5 seconds after opening, in every theme (12 page views stacked at the same spot). The reader auditor measured the pre-built page turn at 1% opacity (not visible). Two auditors disagree, so this needs a look on your phone before anyone touches the page turn, which is a locked area.
findings.where: Reader header, 390 day (Aurora, Cypress, Newsprint shots) · prepTurn www/index.html:8670 · #rd .book .view stacking
findings.why: If it shows on a phone it looks like a rendering fault on every story.
findings.fix: If confirmed: make the pre-built pages fully hidden (visibility or opacity 0) until the turn starts.
findings.risk: High: the page turn is locked (do not retune) and tuned against real-device timing.
findings.noMock: No mockup until confirmed on a phone.

findings.title: Settings search cannot find most theme names
findings.what: Typing "Mono" or "Halcyon" returns "Nothing matches"; "Sepia", "Cypress" and "Pure Black" match only because those words are hand-typed into one synonym list; "Terminal" matches "Theme layouts" by accident. Setting names themselves search fine.
findings.where: Settings home search · SET_SYN www/index.html:10457 · setSearch :10459 indexes only .line rows; the theme picker is not a row
findings.why: Someone who remembers a theme's name is told it does not exist.
findings.fix: Build the synonym string from the theme list itself instead of a hand-typed list; optionally give the theme picker its own search entry.

findings.title: Many controls are smaller than a fingertip
findings.what: Many tap targets are under 44×44px: every settings switch is 52×32 and tapping the row's text does nothing; segmented buttons 31-34px tall; pill buttons (Export, Import, Clear, Reset…, Erase everything) 36px; Close/Back 38-40px. On the Daily, the cover's three small buttons are 28px tall, contents links 24px. Nothing overlaps; the controls are just small.
findings.where: .tg www/index.html:206 · .segs button :211 · .srst :2068 · .dexp :3279 · .cl :2896 · identical at 390/884
findings.why: Small switches are hard to hit for exactly the readers a "bigger buttons" option exists for.
findings.fix: CSS only: a minimum 44px hit area (an invisible padding ring, as the sort rows already do), or let a tap on the label toggle its switch.
findings.risk: Low for hit rings; medium if heights change.

findings.title: "Clear downloaded stories" acts instantly, no confirm, no Undo
findings.what: Every other destructive control (Erase everything, Reset appearance, Remove a site, Reset this section, Clear history) asks first or offers Undo. This one acts on the tap.
findings.where: Settings › Downloads and Storage › Advanced · #clr click www/index.html:12436 · row :4882
findings.why: One stray tap throws away every story downloaded for offline reading, often with no connection to get them back.
findings.fix: Wrap it in the existing confirm box ("Clear downloaded stories?" Clear / Keep them), like Remove a site.

findings.title: Web version sends each background download to all four relays
findings.what: On the web (not Android, which reads sites directly), every story pre-downloaded in the background is sent through all four public relays one after another, not just the first that works: 5 sites made 165 requests on one cold Daily load (40 stories × 4 routes). Cause: in background mode the winning route waits out a 6-second quiet gate before it reports success, while the 650ms stagger timer keeps launching the next relay. The privacy page says public relays are used only "if that fails", which is true for Android and for stories you open, not for this path. One story also contacted the Jina reader at the same instant as the first relay rather than as a fallback.
findings.where: fetchText1 www/index.html:5201-5255 (gate at :5236 before res(t) :5238; stagger in start() :5244) · getFull(a.link,true) from pump :9538 · bgGate :5131 · privacy.html lines 43 and 45
findings.why: Each story address is handed to three outside services instead of one, and the browser does four times the network work.
findings.fix: When a usable body arrives, stop the stagger timer and abort the other routes before waiting on the quiet gate (a "won" flag the launcher checks).
findings.risk: Medium: shared fetch race; run the prefetch/relay tests.
findings.noMock: No mockup: network behavior (request logs in the audit folder).

findings.title: Masthead title clips the tail of the "y"
findings.what: "The Daily" in the top bar is cut at the bottom (content 28px tall in a 24px box with overflow hidden), at normal and large text sizes and at 884.
findings.where: .top h1 www/index.html:812 (#ttl)
findings.why: A chopped letter on a magazine masthead looks like a bug.
findings.fix: A touch more line height or 3px of bottom padding.
findings.risk: Low (header 4px taller; check the docked tabs).

findings.title: Add a site: the error message is far below the field
findings.what: A non-address shows a clear message ("That doesn't look like a web address…") but 408px below the field, under the Starter packs / Near you / Browse topics cards. Screen readers hear it; sighted readers may not connect it to the field.
findings.where: #err in #dlg, 390 night · handler www/index.html:11283
findings.why: The reader types again without seeing why it failed.
findings.fix: Move the message directly under the field's hint line.

findings.title: Nothing says you are offline on a warm start
findings.what: Open the app with stored stories and no connection: the Daily and All Stories show the stored stories as if fresh. No pill, no banner. The "Offline" pill next to the title exists but only for the user-chosen Offline mode, not for an actual lost connection. A cold start with no stored stories handles it well.
findings.where: body.offl #ttl::after www/index.html:678 · offApply :6146 · online/offline listeners :5841/:8221 never set a class
findings.why: On a train with no signal the reader waits for new stories that cannot come and blames the sites.
findings.fix: On the browser's offline/online events (and at boot) toggle a second class that reuses the same pill.

findings.title: "Reset this section" has no Undo; two spellings of offline
findings.what: "Reset this section" asks for a second tap but offers no Undo, while "Reset appearance and reading settings" and the Quick setup presets do. Also "You are offline" (empty page) vs "You're offline" (messages).
findings.where: setReset www/index.html:10475 · empNoStories :12138
findings.why: Consistency; a reset you did not mean is unrecoverable.
findings.fix: Snapshot the keys and offer Undo in the message, copied from the appearance reset; pick one spelling.
findings.noMock: No mockup: identical to the existing preset Undo message.

findings.title: The Daily loads forever when every site failed
findings.what: When every site has answered but none delivered a story (offline on first run, or feeds that return nothing), the Daily keeps its loading skeleton ("Gathering the day's stories from 3 sites…") indefinitely. All Stories on the same data shows a proper "Your sites didn't answer / You are offline" page with Refresh. The web build swaps the caption after 8 seconds, but the Android app would spin.
findings.where: renderToday www/index.html:8312-8313 and 8370-8371 · skelCap :14851
findings.why: A first-time reader on a flaky connection never learns that nothing could be fetched or what to do.
findings.fix: When nothing is still loading and there are no stories, fall through to the same honest empty page All Stories uses.
findings.risk: Low-medium: touches the Daily's empty branch.

findings.title: The list/tiles button does nothing on the Daily
findings.what: The top-bar layout button ("Show list" / "Show tiles") is shown on the Daily, changes its icon when tapped, and changes nothing else: the page is pixel-identical. It only has an effect on All Stories, a site or a folder.
findings.where: #vw www/index.html:4855 area · hidden only for Saved/History/Stats/Highlights at :6339
findings.why: A button that changes its icon but nothing else looks broken and teaches the reader that icons here may be dead.
findings.fix: Hide it on the Daily the same way Mark-all is hidden on Saved and History.

findings.title: ALL-CAPS headlines turn the "Developing" strip into nonsense
findings.what: A shouting headline ("WHY THE WHOLE INDUSTRY IS SUDDENLY TALKING ABOUT BATTERIES AGAIN") fills the Developing strip with capitalized common words as topics: "WHOLE 3 · INDUSTRY 3 · SUDDENLY…". The strip treats capitalized words as names.
findings.where: trendStripHtml www/index.html:6580 and the word counter upstream
findings.why: The first row of the page suggests "WHOLE" is a developing story.
findings.fix: Lower-case titles that are mostly uppercase before counting, or require a word to be capitalized in two differently-cased titles.

findings.title: Searching one letter offers to follow or mute "Z" as a topic
findings.what: Typing one letter into Search turns the results page into a "TOPIC · Z" header with Follow / Mute / Close topic buttons and "24 stories across 3 sites" (every story containing the letter matches).
findings.where: Search, 390 · topic masthead .tmast around www/index.html:14960
findings.why: A first-time reader does not know what a topic is yet; offering to follow the letter Z looks absurd.
findings.fix: Only build the topic header when the query is at least 3 characters or one whole word.

findings.title: The reader's colored dot is secretly the "Go to site" button
findings.what: In the reader's top bar, the bare colored dot next to Back is a button ("Go to The Verge") that leaves for the publisher's website. It reads as a status light; nothing says it is tappable or where it goes.
findings.where: Reader, 390 · the .bs button with aria-label "Go to <site>" in #rd
findings.why: Curious taps bounce the reader out to a browser; readers who want the source never find it.
findings.fix: Show the site name (or an arrow) beside the dot as a small pill, or move "Go to site" into the More menu.

findings.title: First-screen words that assume you already know the app
findings.what: On day one the cover says "VOL. 26 · NO. 303" with a giant ghost 303, blocks are labeled "AFTER DINNER · THE VERGE" and "LATE WORD · ARS TECHNICA", the All Stories chip says "Smart", and "Sections / Cards / Columns" are unexplained.
